replies.text:
Check against commonly-missed threats:

- Automated abuse (brute force, email/SMS flooding, mass sign-up, scraping): design has no sign-in form, no messaging, no public endpoint — only "Support admins can click "log in as customer"", exposure "internal". Not present.
- Staff/admin screens showing other people's content: the admin holds a customer session ("The feature issues a customer session to the admin"), not a privileged console view of user content; no comments, files, tickets or profile fields are named. Not present.
- Privileged actions without a record of who did it: present — "The feature issues a customer session to the admin" with nothing naming an actor record; already covered by listed threat 3 (Repudiation, "nothing records which employee was behind them").
- Cacheable personal/financial pages (browser, proxy, CDN): design names no documents, downloads or caching surface. Not present.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails, headers or another system: no export, log-write or email path stated. Not present.
- Single-reviewer threats: the spoofing items (#1, #2) are the same mechanism and same takeover harm as listed threat 1; #3 is a sub-case of listed threat 5; #4 is a restatement of listed threat 6; #5 ("may trust a client-supplied customer id") and #6 (session-state collision) depend on how the feature is built, which the design does not state. None qualify.
